blocks.heading: Mark up
blocks.text: Mark up = gross profit / cost of sales × 100. It expresses gross profit relative to the cost of goods sold, whereas gross margin uses sales revenue as its denominator. The percentages differ even for the same transaction. Mark up is not the increase in total net profit and does not account for all other operating expenses. Retain full working and round the final percentage to two decimal places.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Neri has gross profit N$96,000 and cost of sales N$144,000. Mark up = 96,000 / 144,000 × 100, rounded to 66.67%. The 40.00% gross margin uses sales N$240,000 instead, so it is not interchangeable with mark up.

blocks.heading: Debtors collection period
blocks.text: Debtors collection period = debtors / credit sales × 365 days for annual credit sales. It estimates how many days of credit sales are represented by the debtors balance. A longer period can mean cash is tied up longer and collection needs attention, but sales patterns and agreed terms also matter. Use credit sales, not total sales when the two differ. Use year-end debtors unless average figures are specified.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Neri has year-end debtors N$18,000 and annual credit sales N$219,000. Collection period = 18,000 / 219,000 × 365 = 30.00 days. The balance represents about thirty days of annual credit sales, not proof that every customer pays on day thirty.

blocks.heading: Creditors payment period
blocks.text: Creditors payment period = creditors / credit purchases × 365 days for annual credit purchases. It estimates how long payment to suppliers is taking relative to the purchases base. Longer payment can conserve cash temporarily but may damage supplier confidence, interrupt supplies or lose discounts if it breaches agreed terms. A shorter period can indicate prompt payment but may use cash before necessary. Judge against terms, not a universal preference for the longest period.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Neri has year-end creditors N$20,000 and annual credit purchases N$146,000. Payment period = 20,000 / 146,000 × 365 = 50.00 days. Compare the fifty-day estimate with supplier terms before calling it good or bad.
